b.x: North-east monsoon and Tamil Nadu
The winter high over NW India sends winds NW → SE down the plains; over the Bay of Bengal they become the **north-east monsoon** and pick up moisture.

The **Tamil Nadu / Coromandel coast** gets its **main rain in October–December (Nov–Dec)** from the NE monsoon; South Arcot and Ramanathapuram get **over 50%** of their rain then. It also reaches **Rayalaseema, Nellore, south coastal AP, SE Karnataka, SE Kerala** – the Gujarat coast gets none.

**Why Tamil Nadu is dry in the SW monsoon:** it lies in the **rain shadow** of the Western Ghats for the Arabian Sea branch, and the Bay branch blows **parallel to the coast** – so **Chennai** gets the least SW-monsoon rain among Kolkata, Mangalore, Chennai and Delhi.
